newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Philippine Navy has arrested at least 23 Chinese fishermen off the disputed Spartly Islands in the South China Sea, officials say. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The military has placed spies in every local exchange of the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co to do surveillance work on opposition leaders, a PLDT union official says. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The government is fast-tracking irrigation and other water management projects around the country to mitigate the effects of El Nino, Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero says. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- Socialite Baby Arenas dismisses the accusation made by Senator Miriam Defenso Santiago that she is trying to influence the Supreme Court to allow a citizens' group to call a plebiscite which will allow President Fidel Ramos to extend his term. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Volume at the Philipine Dealing System goes beyond the $100-million mark for the first time since six foreign banks are allowed to trade in the electronic exchange. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- An international investment research firm affirms the soundness of Philippine economic fundamentals as it urges investors to hold on to their pesos. (TODAY)
- Several Build-Operate-Transfer projects have been exempted by the Board of Investments from the mandatory initial public offering. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- The Philippines may not be able to meet its commitment to export sugar to the United States, National Food Authority administrator Joemari Gerochi says. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
